questions.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z<-0.35).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.4\,$ | $\,0.3264\,$ | $\,0.3228\,$ | $\,0.3192\,$ |
| $\,-0.3\,$ | $\,0.3632\,$ | $\,0.3594\,$ | $\,0.3557\,$ |
| $\,-0.2\,$ | $\,0.4013\,$ | $\,0.3974\,$ | $\,0.3936\,$ |

$P(Z<-0.35)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
If $Z∼N(0,1),$ then by the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Also, since $Z$ is continuous, 

$$
P(Z<-0.35)=P(Z\le -0.35)=Φ(-0.35).
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/ab5be5e655c8daad36f35bee1abf3c82e3766b734da928be3dd060db551fbbb9.png)

Now, we determine the value of $Φ(-0.35)$ from the table:

- We first select the row that corresponds to $-0.3$ and the column that corresponds to $0.05.$

- Then, we take the value that lies at the intersection:

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.4\,$ | $\,0.3264\,$ | $\,0.3228\,$ | $\,0.3192\,$ |
| $\,-0.3\,$ | $\,0.3632\,$ | $\,0.3594\,$ | $\,0.3557\,$ |
| $\,-0.2\,$ | $\,0.4013\,$ | $\,0.3974\,$ | $\,0.3936\,$ |

Therefore, according to the table, we have

$$
P(Z\le -0.35)=Φ(-0.35)=0.3632.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z\ge 0.17).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/759e123d5c61321e78b085260a14d5ae98a54b724b82b06cdecc46ff28072b8b.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 0.17) & =1-P(Z<0.17) \\  & =1-Φ(0.17)\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/83ab5f91c5ee81eeb4c31b42558af5c46cb59d74603b30913ab80dadeafc3317.png)

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(0.17)=0.5675.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 0.17) & =1-Φ(0.17) \\  & =1-0.5675 \\  & =0.4325.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on a Bounded Interval
questions.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(0.1<Z<1.5).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/806631e940119accaf9fa2dd9e52e59f4ae16480f237c2bb67ddc7796e4967c0.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.1<Z<1.5) & =P(Z<1.5)-P(Z\le 0.1) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.5)-P(Z\le 0.1) \\  & =Φ(1.5)-Φ(0.1).\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.1) & =0.5398 \\ Φ(1.5) & =0.9332\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.1<Z<1.5) & =Φ(1.5)-Φ(0.1) \\  & =0.9332-0.5398 \\  & =0.3934.\end{aligned}
$$
